children: Shares of Bajaj Finance Ltd. gained as much as 5% on Monday, October 5, in response to its September quarter business update, following which, brokerage firm JPMorgan also raised its price target on the stock.
The stock has snapped a four-day losing streak in the process, making an intraday high of ₹995. The stock had declined in seven out of the last 10 trading sessions.

For the September quarter, Bajaj Finance's customer franchise stood at 128.85 million, a growth of 4.42 million compared to the June quarter. The figure during the same quarter last year stood at 110.64 million.

New loans booked by Bajaj Finance during the quarter stood at 13.45 million, a growth of 11% from last year. During the June quarter, the figure stood at 12.17 million. Volume growth, according to Bajaj Finance, is not comparable due to the early onset of the festive season last year

Bajaj Finance's Assets Under Management (AUM) stood at ₹5.84 lakh crore at the end of the quarter, compared to ₹4.62 lakh crore last year. During the quarter, Bajaj Finance's AUM grew by ₹37,800 crore during the July-September period. Deposit book stood at ₹69,750 crore.

The board of Bajaj Finance, before the disclosure of its provisional business update, had approved raising funds to the tune of nearly ₹18,000 crore. This includes ₹11,700 crore, that will be raised through a Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP), and another ₹5,800 crore, which will be raised through a preferential warrants to promoter Bajaj Finserv.
JPMorgan Raises Bajaj Finance Share Price Target
JPMorgan retained its "overweight" rating on Bajaj Finance and revised its price target higher to ₹1,310 from ₹1,295 earlier.
The brokerage said that growth appears broad-based across segments and that the strong momentum is only expected to sustain over the upcoming quarters.
Bajaj Finance may even upgrade its financial year 2027 growth guidance, after the business update, JPMorgan wrote in its note.
Jefferies Calls Bajaj Finance a Top Pick

Jefferies has maintained its "buy" rating on Bajaj Finance with a price target of ₹1,280. It said that a strong 23% loan growth and stake monetization in Bajaj Housing Finance may have driven this decision.
The capital raise could lift Bajaj Finance's Book Value per share (BVPS) by 8%, while its EPS could remain broadly flat, as per Jefferies, and Return on Equity could taper marginally.
However, Jefferies still called Bajaj Finance its top pick.

39 analysts have coverage on Bajaj Finance, of which 28 have a "buy" rating, seven say "hold", and four have a "sell" rating on the stock. The consensus estimates of price targets implies an upside potential of 22% from current levels.
Shares of Bajaj Finance are trading 3.7% higher on Monday at ₹983.3. With this move, the stock has turned positive on a year-to-date basis.

title: Bajaj Finance share price target raised by JPMorgan after Q2 update; Stock turns positive YTD
